summary: Let S be the 𝔬-algebra generated by the substitutions, into the rescaled linear forms ι(δ̄)⁻¹·ℓ_i, of the series in 𝔬[[φ]], of L′ and of exp(−L) (θ = exp(−L)). Every element of S has integral constant term and S is closed under ∂_x; hence jets along integral polynomials of elements of S are integral. Each factor of the product lies in S, because U_yθ(δ̄z) = θ(z)^N·u(z) with u ∈ 𝔬[[φ]] (δ̄ is an isogeny).

steps.claim: In ℂ_p: θ = exp(−L) with L(0) = L′(0) = 0, L″ = L₂ + ξ (ξ = Taylor series of ℘(z+t) − ℘(t)), |ιₚ(i√d)·L₂| ≤ 1, and the 𝔬[[φ]]-memberships of `CMLattice.exists_log_theta`.
steps.lean: 1 (y i) C.θ)).subst (linearSeries (c i))) ∈ valRingCp p := have ⟨L, _, l⟩ := C.exists_log_theta

steps.claim: For every i, the series ιₚ(δ̄)⁻¹·∑_x c_{i,x}z_x can be substituted (no constant term).
steps.lean: have s i : HasSubst ((ιₚ (conj δ))⁻¹ • linearSeries (c i)) := by simp

steps.claim: Let S be the 𝔬-subalgebra of ℂ_p[[z]] generated by f(ιₚ(δ̄)⁻¹ℓ_i) for all i and all f in 𝔬[[φ]] ∪ {L′, exp(−L)}.
steps.lean:
let S := adjoin (valRingCp p)
    {f.substAlgHom (s i) | (i) (f ∈ C.phiSeriesRing.carrier ∪ {d⁄dX L, expSubst (-L)})}
have m {i f} hf : _ ∈ S := subset_adjoin ⟨i, f, hf, rfl⟩

steps.claim: h: every F ∈ S has integral constant term, and ∂_x F ∈ S for every variable x.
steps.lean:
have h {F} : F ∈ S → F.constantCoeff ∈ valRingCp p ∧ ∀ x, F.pderiv x ∈ S := by
    apply adjoin_induction
    rintro _ ⟨i, f, hf, ⟨⟩⟩
    simp [coe_substAlgHom]
    refine .imp_right (fun (h : (d • d⁄dX f).substAlgHom (s i) ∈ S) x ↦ ?_) ?_
    simpa [subst, linearSeries, MvPowerSeries.pderiv_X, coe_substAlgHom,
      ← Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul ℂ_[p], ← smul_assoc] using! S.smul_mem h ⟨_, k ..⟩
    obtain g | ⟨⟨⟩⟩ := hf
    use (C.isSeriesGenerator_translatedWpDeriv.norm_coeff_le_one g).1, by simp [*,
      C.deriv_mem_phiSeriesRing g]
    use by simp [*, ← coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff, coeff_derivative], m (.inl ?_)
    simpa [*, ↓← mul_assoc, ↓← sq, ↓map_sqrt_neg_sq, smul_eq_C_mul, add_mem_cancel_right,
      taylorVia_translatedWp_mem_phiSeriesRing] using
      C.isSeriesGenerator_translatedWpDeriv.smul_mem ((valRingCp p).mul_mem
      (C.norm_le_one_of_isogeny (C.5 (sqrt_neg_mem_quadInt _))) l.2.2.2.2.1) (one_mem _)
    repeat simp_all [algebraMap_eq_smul_one, S, derivative_subst]
steps.typed_fact: F ∈ S → F.constantCoeff ∈ valRingCp p ∧ ∀ x, F.pderiv x ∈ S

steps.claim: Generator case: F = f(ιₚ(δ̄)⁻¹ℓ_i) with f ∈ 𝔬[[φ]] ∪ {L′, exp(−L)}.

By the chain rule ∂_x F = f′(ιₚ(δ̄)⁻¹ℓ_i)·c_{i,x}/ιₚ(δ̄) = (d·f′)(ιₚ(δ̄)⁻¹ℓ_i)·(c_{i,x}/(ιₚ(δ̄)d)), so ∂_x F ∈ S follows from (d·f′)(ιₚ(δ̄)⁻¹ℓ_i) ∈ S; it remains to show that and the integrality of f(0).
steps.lean: refine .imp_right (fun (h : (d • d⁄dX f).substAlgHom (s i) ∈ S) x ↦ ?_) ?_

steps.claim: The chain-rule computation, using that c_{i,x}/(ιₚ(δ̄)d) ∈ 𝔬 (hypothesis k) and S is an 𝔬-module.
steps.lean:
simpa [subst, linearSeries, MvPowerSeries.pderiv_X, coe_substAlgHom,
      ← Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul ℂ_[p], ← smul_assoc] using! S.smul_mem h ⟨_, k ..⟩

steps.claim: Cases: f ∈ 𝔬[[φ]], or f is L′ or exp(−L).
If f ∈ 𝔬[[φ]]: f(0) is integral (`norm_coeff_le_one` of the series generator) and f′ ∈ 𝔬[[φ]] (`deriv_mem_phiSeriesRing`), hence d·f′ ∈ 𝔬[[φ]], so (d·f′)(ιₚ(δ̄)⁻¹ℓ_i) is a generator of S.
steps.lean:
use (C.isSeriesGenerator_translatedWpDeriv.norm_coeff_le_one g).1, by simp [*,
      C.deriv_mem_phiSeriesRing g]

steps.claim: If f = L′: L′(0) = 0 (L₁ = 0) is integral; it remains that d·L″ ∈ 𝔬[[φ]].
steps.lean: use by simp [*, ← coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff, coeff_derivative], m (.inl ?_)

steps.claim: d·L″ = d·L₂ + d·ξ ∈ 𝔬[[φ]]: d·L₂ = −(√−d)·(√−d·L₂) with |ιₚ(√−d)·L₂| ≤ 1 and ιₚ(√−d) integral (`norm_le_one_of_isogeny`, √−d ∈ 𝓞_K), and ξ ∈ 𝔬[[φ]] (`taylorVia_translatedWp_mem_phiSeriesRing`).
steps.lean:
simpa [*, ↓← mul_assoc, ↓← sq, ↓map_sqrt_neg_sq, smul_eq_C_mul, add_mem_cancel_right,
      taylorVia_translatedWp_mem_phiSeriesRing] using
      C.isSeriesGenerator_translatedWpDeriv.smul_mem ((valRingCp p).mul_mem
      (C.norm_le_one_of_isogeny (C.5 (sqrt_neg_mem_quadInt _))) l.2.2.2.2.1) (one_mem _)

steps.claim: The remaining cases: f = exp(−L) (constant term 1, derivative −L′·exp(−L) ∈ S) and the induction steps for constants, sums and products (Leibniz rule).

For every F ∈ S, the jet of F along ιₚ(Q) is integral: induction on the polynomial Q (constants give the constant term of F; multiplying Q by a variable z_x replaces F by ∂_x F, `jet_mul_X`), using h.
steps.lean:
(by apply Q.induction_on <;> simp_all [jet_mul_X, ← MvPolynomial.monomial_zero'] : ∀ F ∈ S, jet _
  _ F ∈ _)

steps.claim: The product lies in S: δ̄ ∈ 𝓞_K defines an isogeny of degree N = |δ|², and δy_i ∈ Λ, so U_{y_i}θ(ιₚ(δ̄)z) = θ(z)^N·u_i(z) with u_i ∈ 𝔬[[φ]] (`rescale_translate_eq_theta_pow_mul`); substituting z = ιₚ(δ̄)⁻¹ℓ_i, each factor is exp(−L)^N∘(ιₚ(δ̄)⁻¹ℓ_i) times u_i∘(ιₚ(δ̄)⁻¹ℓ_i), a product of generators.
steps.lean:
_ (prod_mem fun i ↦ (C.rescale_translate_eq_theta_pow_mul
    (exists_isIsogeny_of_mul_mem_lattice (C.5 (conj_mem_quadInt u))).choose_spec h0 (w i)).elim
  fun _ ⟨_, e⟩ ↦ by simpa [coe_substAlgHom, h0] using congr(substAlgHom (s i) $e ∈ S).ge (by aesop))
